## TL;DR

Done now starts collapsed for a browser with no saved collapse preference, and mounts no cards while collapsed. Expanded Done keeps at most 40 cards mounted, with scroll spacers and measured card heights. The default can be changed in General settings; a saved browser preference wins.

## Work and rationale

The bounded window uses the column's scroll position, estimated heights for unseen cards, and ResizeObserver measurements for cards already seen. Overscan keeps nearby cards mounted. Done keeps its full count and all tasks stay in the store, so global search still sees old tasks. Keyboard navigation already consults mounted card elements. The default sort is recent; the explicit current-order mode also orders Done by recent completion. Fresh unacknowledged completions expand the column. Config loads before the board so the new default is available before collapse defaults are persisted.

The baseline and after measurements used `.repoos/bench-done-v2.mjs`: the finite UI smoke harness, headless Chromium, 1440×900 viewport, fresh browser context each run, and an intercepted board response with 1,000 synthetic old Done tasks. Each value below is the median of three runs. Board paint is the first animation frame after a MutationObserver sees the Done column; interactive is elapsed navigation to the board plus two frames, a readiness proxy rather than a direct input-latency measurement. Expansion is click to two frames, and scroll is setting scrollTop to the end to two frames. Heap uses Chromium's rounded `performance.memory.usedJSHeapSize`, not a heap snapshot. The browser bundle was rebuilt from the original sources for the baseline and from this tree for the after run. Network and CPU were not throttled.

| Metric | Before | After | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Board paint | 2,424 ms | 1,160 ms | -52.1% |
| Readiness proxy | 3,144 ms | 1,387 ms | -55.9% |
| Done cards at load | 1,000 | 0 | -100% |
| Board DOM descendants | 17,053 | 53 | -99.7% |
| JS heap after load | 139 MB | 13.4 MB | -90.4% |
| Expand Done | 799 ms | 565 ms | -29.3% |
| Scroll to end | 202 ms | 259 ms | +28.2% |

These synthetic timings vary considerably between runs; the scroll measurement worsened and is particularly short and noisy. The test fixture is not a measurement of real network transfer or the 2.6 MB production payload. Rendering reduction is substantial, but the evidence does not establish that server-side pagination is worth its complexity; revisit with real payload and slow-network measurements if load remains a problem.

## Approaches tried

A preliminary benchmark used recent synthetic tasks and measured page paint rather than board paint. That sample was discarded for the comparison above. The final fixture uses old timestamps so the fresh-completion auto-expand behavior does not defeat the default-collapse scenario. No virtual-scroll dependency was added.

## Challenges and blockers

Card heights vary, so a fixed-height virtual list would misrepresent positions. The implementation estimates unseen heights and replaces estimates as cards are mounted. This makes the scrollbar an estimate until cards have been measured. Browser preference, live completion, and config startup ordering require separate handling.

## Key learnings

The initial cost was dominated by the rendered tree in this fixture. Eliminating mounted cards in collapsed Done and bounding the expanded slice reduces that tree without removing tasks from search or the board payload. The performance data cannot predict actual user network latency.
